items.title: Bill Holman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: I assume that that is slightly different from Mozart eighth notes.

ctx.x: Yeah. They’ve got a string section, it’s a fairly good size, it’s almost 30 strings, and they’re very enthusiastic and very cooperative. Most string players don’t want to hear about playing jazz. They don’t even like contemporary classical music. But these guys can actually swing a little bit. They can do two types the [scats] kind of swing, and the straight-eighth thing, which is a very subtle thing that a lot of horn players are not familiar with. But these guys do it and they volunteer to do it. Because I had…
Yeah. Turtle Island also. They swing pretty good. But you said something about straight eighth notes. How do you mean that? I assume that that is slightly different from Mozart eighth notes.

Yeah. Well I usually consider real straight eighth notes as rock & roll [scats] that’s very strict. But there’s a way, like you’ve got a rhythm section that’s playing a triplet feel [scats] a horn line could go [scats]. It’s not quite straight but it’s not a triplet feel either. And unless you were raised with it, like I was, it’s a very hard thing to pick up. And these guys can do it.
